headline: LungIMPACT randomized trial finds no significant pathway-time benefit from immediate AI prioritization of primary-care chest X-rays
summary: The prospective, multicentre LungIMPACT randomized controlled trial compared immediate qXR AI worklist prioritization with usual reporting for adult primary-care chest X-rays across five NHS trusts in England. AI decision support was available in both arms; the randomized intervention was when the AI alert arrived. Of 97,731 CXRs, 93,326 were analyzed. The peer-reviewed report found no statistically significant difference in time to CT (median 53 days in both groups) or lung-cancer diagnosis (44 versus 46 days), and no significant differences in referral, treatment timing or stage at diagnosis. This is a bounded result about immediate worklist prioritization in this trial context, not a comparison of AI with no AI or evidence that all AI imaging uses lack value.
